hints: Integrate $\frac{dy}{dx} = ax^2 + bx - 4$ to get $y = \frac{1}{3}ax^3 + \frac{1}{2}bx^2 - 4x + c$.
walkthrough:
Integrate the derivative with respect to $x$:
$$y = \int (ax^2 + bx - 4)\,dx = \frac{1}{3}ax^3 + \frac{1}{2}bx^2 - 4x + c$$

At the stationary point $x = 2$, set the derivative equal to zero:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=2} = 0 \implies a(2^2) + b(2) - 4 = 0 \implies 4a + 2b = 4 \implies 2a + b = 2$$

Substitute the coordinates $(2, 3)$ into the curve equation:
$$3 = \frac{1}{3}a(2^3) + \frac{1}{2}b(2^2) - 4(2) + 11 = \frac{8}{3}a + 2b - 8 + 11 = \frac{8}{3}a + 2b + 3$$
$$\frac{8}{3}a + 2b = 0 \implies 4a + 3b = 0$$

Solve the simultaneous linear equations in $a$ and $b$:
$$b = 2 - 2a \implies 4a + 3(2 - 2a) = 0 \implies 4a + 6 - 6a = 0 \implies 2a = 6 \implies a = 3$$
$$b = 2 - 2(3) = -4$$
$$a = 3, \quad b = -4$$
